1.explanation: All of the tooltip display logic flows through the core tooltip implementation and the React wrappers around it. 1) tooltip.js (in components) defines the low-level show/hide events for focus and hover; it currently enables the tooltip on both focus and hover without coordination. 2) Tooltip.js (React) is the primary React component that subscribes to focus and mouse events and renders the portal; it doesn’t suppress a focus tooltip when a hover tooltip appears elsewhere. 3) TooltipIcon.js wraps a single icon button with Tooltip.js, adding focus behavior for icon-only buttons. Because the overlapping tooltips occur only on icon-only buttons, adjusting or augmenting the show/hide logic in these three files will let you hide the focused tooltip when another icon-only button is hovered (or remove the focus-trigger rule altogether for icon-only scenarios).
1.bug_scenario: When you have two icon-only buttons side-by-side, the first button’s tooltip remains visible once it has focus, and when you hover over the second button its tooltip also appears. You end up with two overlapping tooltips – one for the focused button and one for the hovered button. The desired behavior is that once you hover a different icon-only button, the first (focused) button’s tooltip should hide.

2.explanation:
All three files live in the vanilla-JS tooltip module, which is responsible for wiring up show/hide events on icon-only buttons. 

• tooltip--simple.js implements the behavior for the small, arrow-tipped tooltips used on icon-only triggers. It listens for focus and mouseenter, showing a tooltip without hiding any others.

• tooltip.js is the more general tooltip engine (used by programmatic tooltips) and contains similar focus/hover logic for its widgets.

• tooltip.config.js defines the selectors and event hooks for initializing both tooltip systems. Because focus-triggered tooltips aren’t automatically torn down when you hover a new trigger, you end up with two active tooltips. Adjusting the focus/hover handlers in these files (for example, hiding any open tooltip before showing a new one, or disabling focus-triggered show on icon-only buttons) will resolve the overlap issue.
2.bug_scenario: After clicking (or keyboard-focusing) an icon-only button, its tooltip is shown on focus. Then when you hover over a neighboring icon-only button, its tooltip also appears—but the first tooltip (still “focused”) isn’t hidden. The two tooltips now overlap, which is confusing to users and breaks the one-tooltip-at-a-time expectation.
